ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Kingdom sanctions list, and Samoa domestic designated persons and terrorist financing lists; mandatory enhanced due diligence for all politically exposed persons, immediate family members, and close associates; risk-based transactional monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit within statutory timeframes; full audit-trail retention aligned with the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering mutual evaluation obligations and the High_Risk_Special_License classification for Multi-Family Office discretionary portfolio advisory services.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry - Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; official online filing portal accessed exclusively through licensed Samoan registered agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Latin script and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; a parallel Chinese-language name may be recorded in the charter and ancillary certificates as a translation, but it does not replace the registered Latin-script name. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing domestic or international company name on the Samoan registry, and must not imply any licensable banking, trust, insurance, or fiduciary activity without prior regulatory consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the licensed registered agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and proposed compliance. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister for Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 calendar days of the reconsideration decision. The Minister's determination may be challenged by judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa. A rejected applicant may also file a fresh name application with a revised name at any time after the expiration of the rejection notice period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only insofar as the designated licensed Samoan registered agent maintains a physical registered office on the islands of Upolu or Savai'i, Samoa, and the company retains a substantive agent-presence and statutory records location in Samoa; a purely virtual office with no on-island registered agent and no statutory records repository will not satisfy the International Companies Act 2019 registered office requirement, will fail the economic substance declaration, and will jeopardize the High_Risk_Special_License fit-and-proper assessment for Multi-Family Office discretionary portfolio advisory services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: approximately 55% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit or the Samoa International Finance Authority within the first 24 months of incorporation, driven by the High_Risk_Special_License AML/CFT risk tier, the Asia/Pacific Group mutual evaluation cycle, and the discretionary portfolio advisory scope over Swift interbank and custody wire payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1988 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; principally Part II ss. 6-9 (incorporation and certificate), s. 12 (registered office and registered agent), ss. 20-21 (directors and officers), and Part V s. 73 (licensed international company activities, including Multi-Family Office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Constitution) together with Form 1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company, certified by a licensed registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act 1988; shares may be issued with or without par value and in any currency, with no escrow or capital verification requirement at incorporation. For the Multi-Family Office licence, the applicant must separately demonstrate adequate initial capital/resources to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority under the MFO Licensing Framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share subscription is approved; shares subscribed are allotted, the issue price is credited as paid-up, and the share register is authorized for entry. RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the Registered Agent's office in Apia, Samoa, and the Registered Agent is appointed to maintain the register and receive service of process. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed first Director and [Name] is appointed Secretary, each to serve without remuneration until the next annual general meeting or until removal. RESOLVED that the corporate seal, authorized signatories and banking mandates are adopted, and the Director is instructed to file the Multi-Family Office application with the Financial Services Regulatory Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of licensed registered agent and corporate name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Registered Agent; International Companies Registry, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Samoan-licensed registered agent and instruct the submission of two proposed company names for availability check. The agent certifies that the proposed name is not undesirable, does not conflict with existing Samoan or international companies, and does not imply a prohibited activity.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner
Bank reference or due diligence questionnaire
Two proposed company names
Registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused by the Registry, submit an alternative name immediately; if refusal appears erroneous, lodge a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days under the International Companies Act 1988.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the Act, obtain subscriber signatures, notarize or verify signature pages, and have the registered agent certify the solvency and legal capacity of the subscribers and first directors.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act of each first director and secretary
Certified passport copies of subscribers and officers
Draft initial share subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requires corrective wording, the registered agent may effect minor amendments without re-notarization; any substantive amendment requires re-execution by the subscribers and fresh notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application with the International Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: International Companies Registry, MCIL (counter in Apia or authorized online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 together with the executed constitution, the registered agent's certificate of registered office, officer consents, and the prescribed filing fee. The Registry examines the documents for statutory compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Application for Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent's certificate of registered office in Apia
Consent forms of initial directors and secretary
Government filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent responds to the Registry requisition within five business days with corrective documents or formal submissions; if the defect is fundamental, withdraw and refile with amended documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and first governance formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful filing, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The directors then convene the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, open the company registers, allot shares, and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Pro-forma first board resolution
Share Register and Register of Directors and Secretary
Registered office notice and agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any register omission or defective officer entry is cured by filing a corrective return or a special resolution amendment with the Registrar and noting the date of rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises setup, occupational clearances and Multi-Family Office licence pre-application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA); Samoa Fire & Emergency Services Authority; Planning and Urban Management Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a physical office in Apia and execute a commercial lease. Submit the FSRA Multi-Family Office licence application with the business plan, AML/CFT compliance programme, and fit-and-proper declarations of officers. Concurrently obtain the building occupancy certificate and fire safety certification before commencing regulated activities.
required_dossiers: FSRA MFO licence application form
Multi-Family Office business plan and budget
AML/CFT compliance manual and risk assessment
Fit-and-proper declarations for directors and shareholders
Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire & Emergency Services Authority
Building occupancy certificate from Planning and Urban Management Agency
Commercial lease agreement for the Apia office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On an FSRA deficiency letter, respond with supplementary documents within 30 days; if the licence is refused, request reconsideration or appeal under the Financial Services Regulatory Authority Act 2020 while retaining the company in inactive, non-regulated status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), Apia, Samoa, acting with the Samoa International Finance Authority and the International Companies Registry for regulated International Company activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Multi-Family Office (MFO) Licence under the International Companies Act 1988, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018, and the FSRA MFO Licensing Framework

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Environment and Conservation Division, administering the Environment Act 1999
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 5 - Exempt / Administrative office use: no full Environmental Impact Assessment or environmental registration is required for non-industrial financial advisory premises; only the building-permit environmental checklist through the Planning and Urban Management Agency applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions expected. Sanitary wastewater discharge, where sewer connection exists, must meet Samoa Water Authority receiving-water standards (BOD not exceeding 200 mg/L; TSS not exceeding 250 mg/L). E-waste and confidential paper records must be disposed of in compliance with the Waste Management Act 2004 through licensed collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire & Emergency Services Authority; building occupancy and structural load inspection certificate issued under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 by the Planning and Urban Management Agency; workplace clearance and health-and-safety compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2003 of Samoa.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; taxpayer e-services portal 'TAP' (Taxpayer Access Portal) at https://www.revenue.gov.ws; International Company registry administered by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) at https://www.mcil.gov.ws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 with the MCIL Registrar through a licensed Samoa registered agent, filing a charter restricted to offshore business and appointing a registered office in Apia; no minimum capital is required and 100% foreign ownership with non-resident directors is permitted. Step 2: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and company registration number from the Registrar. Step 3: File the exemption application with the Ministry for Revenue (MfR) annexing the Certificate of Incorporation and the offshore-objects charter; the MfR issues a Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming that the IC is outside the scope of Samoan income tax (including the 27% domestic corporate rate) on all non-Samoa-source income, gains and capital. Step 4: The IC is not required to hold an active income-tax TIN because it derives no Samoan-source income; a TIN and VAGST registration are required only if the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa, which is prohibited for ICs in the ordinary course of offshore business. Step 5: If the IC voluntarily engages in zero-rated export activity in Samoa, it may apply to the MfR for VAGST registration to recover input tax, obtaining a separate VAGST TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists in Samoa's domestic law; ICs instead rely on statutory object-based exemption. Available elections: (i) the IC charter's objects clause electing offshore-only activity, which engages the automatic tax immunity in s.202 of the International Companies Act 1987; (ii) a formal application for an Exemption Certificate under s.203 of that Act confirming immunity from income, stamp, land and municipal duties and from the Exchange Control Act 1976; (iii) voluntary VAGST registration for a person making only zero-rated supplies (VAGST Act 2012, s.9); and (iv) no election is available to convert the IC into a Samoa-resident taxable company, because domestic trading is statutorily barred for ICs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax), an invoice-based consumption tax administered by the Ministry for Revenue under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2012
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (VAGST Act 2012, s.7); voluntary registration is available for persons making exclusively zero-rated supplies, e.g. exporters; an International Company confined to offshore business normally falls below this threshold and has no Samoan VAGST nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based clearance mandate, and no digital stamping regime. The statutory compliance obligations are: (i) e-filing of VAGST returns and payments through the MfR Taxpayer Access Portal (TAP); (ii) issuance of prescribed tax invoices under VAGST Act 2012, s.20 showing supplier TIN, recipient TIN for B2B supplies, date, description, consideration, and applicable VAGST status; (iii) seven-year retention of accounting and invoice records; and (iv) electronic filing of export and import declarations through the ASYCUDA World customs clearance platform operated by the Samoa Customs Division.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAGST Act 2012, s.16 zero-rates: (a) exports of goods physically removed from Samoa by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and physically performed entirely outside Samoa; (c) services supplied in connection with land or moveable goods situated outside Samoa; and (d) international freight and passenger transport. A Samoa International Company earning discretionary portfolio-advisory fees from non-resident multi-family clients supplies offshore services that are outside the Samoan VAGST base entirely; should the IC procure goods or local services in Samoa for export, zero-rating is available only with a statutory declaration, corresponding export documentation, and evidence that the 28-day export window has been met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic declaration filed with Samoa Customs Division via ASYCUDA World) in the IC's name
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Airway Bill (air freight) evidencing physical export of the goods from Samoa within 28 days of the time of supply
Commercial Invoice / VAGST Tax Invoice with prescribed content under VAGST Act 2012, s.20, stating the zero rate
VAGST return and zero-rating schedule filed with the Ministry for Revenue, together with the exporter's statutory declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Samoa commercial bank, or SWIFT MT103 payment evidence, proving repatriation of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin and packing/weight lists, where preferential tariff treatment or customs verification requires them
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue audits zero-rated claims by cross-matching ASYCUDA World export declarations with bank-reported foreign exchange receipts, Inward Remittance Certificates, and SWIFT payment trails. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating triggers: default assessments recovering the full 15% VAGST, an accuracy/shortfall penalty of up to 50% of the evaded tax (up to 75% where evasion is intentional), late-payment penalties, and statutory use-of-money interest; refunds obtained by false statements are clawed back retroactively as a debt due with interest. Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 2012 can add fines of up to WST 40,000 and imprisonment, with joint and several liability of directors, and the MfR may also cancel the IC's tax exemption certificate and strike the IC from the International Companies register for serious non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) - Apia, Independent State of Samoa; exchange control administration is shared with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for offshore International Company treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is not freely convertible on the capital account. Current-account transactions (trade in services, operational costs, reasonable management fees) are permitted with supporting vouchers. Capital inflows and outflows, including intercompany funding and profit remittances, require CBS approval for amounts exceeding WST 500,000 and are assessed case-by-case. International Companies (ICs) may maintain fully foreign-currency-denominated accounts in USD, EUR, AUD, and NZD; funds held and settled exclusively in those currencies are freely repatriable without conversion to WST, provided no WST-denominated transactions occur. Profit remittance hurdles: an IC must file a Foreign Exchange Remittance Application, audited annual financial statements (where relevant), a tax clearance from the Ministry of Revenue if triggered, and a board resolution authorising distribution. There is no withholding tax on outbound dividends from an IC, but a 10% levy may apply if the IC is not a licensed financial entity under SIFA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations, the timeline for export receipts is 210 days from shipment date; the mandatory conversion ratio is 100% for domestic exporters unless the Central Bank grants an open foreign-currency retention account. For International Companies with a SIFA special license, there is no mandatory surrender when the receipt is in a currency other than WST and is not part of the domestic export economy. ICs must still submit an annual FX Conversion Certificate and obtain CBS permission for any deposit into a local WST account exceeding WST 100,000 in a single month.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and USD-denominated settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. No licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or virtual banking licence exists in Samoa. Offshore EMIs (Revolut, Wise, Mercury, Airwallex) do not offer onboarding for Samoa-domiciled International Companies because of the absence of a correspondent banking relationship in WST or USD and the elevated money-laundering risk attached to multi-family office structures. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not authorised depository institutions under the Financial Institutions Act 2011; (ii) a funds transfer from an EMI can be rejected at the Samoan receiving bank without an underlying documentary declaration; (iii) use of a Samoan IC with a licensed SIFA trust/family office cannot be supported by an unregulated EMI under FATF Recommendation 15. The only viable treasury rails are SWIFT interbank transfers through a licensed commercial bank in Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for all directors and / or ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of a non-resident International Company. Under CBS FIU guidelines, remote video onboarding is not permitted for a High-Risk Special License (multi-family office). A minimum of one director with signatory authority and the designated compliance officer of the family office must physically attend an interview at the bank's Apia office. The Samoan registered agent and legal counsel may be present but cannot substitute a personal identification. Exceptions are made only for UBOs who are unable to travel due to verified military or medical reasons, and even then the bank requires a golden-file notarisation from a Samoan consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore jurisdiction with no local economic substance; multi-family office acting for multiple unrelated family principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA Special License confirmation; approved substance dossiers evidencing office, board meetings and local compliance officer; consolidated AIFMD-style AML/CFT policies; signed director attestation; a detailed family office investment mandate and service deed listing each participating family.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection for a newly incorporated IC without operating history or audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board resolution; proof of initial share premium via SWIFT MT103 from a known regulated bank; source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO and general partner; legal opinion on IC share issuance; bank reference letters from the last two corresponding banks; pro forma business plan for the multi-family office and regulatory capital sufficiency analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership layer includes a protected trust or SCC (safeguard incorporated cell) with a nominee shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: House of Representatives – certified copy of the registered trust deed; completed CBS Form B-20 'Trust Beneficial Ownership Register'; licensed trustee's KYC summary; fiduciary acknowledgement signed by the Samoan registered agent; a chart showing the chain of ownership to natural persons; independent legal advice certificate confirming AML compliance for trustees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound share capital, share premium or intercompany loan funding must be routed as a wire through a bank outside Samoa (e.g., USD via New York, AUD via Sydney). Use SWIFT MT103 with: field 50K originating regulated entity; field 57A beneficiary bank (e.g., BSP Samoa UPI? BOSPSWSX); field 59 beneficiary account number; in field 72 include `/INV/` with SIFA or IC certificate number. A Foreign Exchange Declaration Form (CBS Form 5B) is required for any credit to a WST account; for pure USD/EUR/AUD accounts, no conversion form is needed but the bank will retain a copy in the EFOSS (Electronic Foreign Exchange Surveillance System). The recipient account must be pre-verified for 'capital injection' classification, and funds must not mix with operational expenses unless the account is dual-purpose. For loans exceeding WST 1,000,000 in value, CBS prior approval must be evidenced by a Bank Reference Number (BRN) issued within 15 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and mandated client asset transfers, the permitted clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary payments; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent reimbursement between Samoan banks and overseas clearing agents; (3) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700/MT710) with confirmed or unconfirmed banker's acceptance for real asset purchases (e.g., real estate, shares); (4) custodian wire via ICSD rails (Clearstream/Euroclear) for securities settlement if the family office holds a professional custody account. Every outbound payment must attach: regulator-approved purpose code (currently 'MFO-OP' for operational expenses, 'MFO-INV' for investment disbursement, 'MFO-FEE' for advisory fees); an FX reference number from the CBS transaction monitoring module; and evidence of underlying contractual obligation (invoice, PPM, subscription agreement). For amounts above USD 250,000, dual control and time-stamped documentary copy in the bank's EFOSS workflow is mandatory.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts (USD/EUR/NZD/AUD/WST) with licensed Samoan commercial banks, up to 2-year tenor, requiring 30% collateral
Cross-currency swaps for intercompany funding maturity matching, approved under CBS Notice No. 4/2023
Currency options purchased (plain vanilla, no short positions; buying or writing requires a separate SIFA high-risk approval)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for WST-only hedging, executed through a correspondent bank outside Samoa, with a monthly reporting obligation to CBS
Participation in the South Pacific FX 'Samoa-NZ/USD Netting Pool' for multi-currency operational consolidations, only for SIFA-licensed family offices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on each anniversary of incorporation; payment accepted up to 30 days after the anniversary date without administrative action
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 10% surcharge; continued non-payment for 90 days triggers administrative strike-off procedures under the International Companies Act 1987

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Beneficial Ownership Register, Registrar of International Companies, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or knowingly filing false information attracts monetary penalties up to USD 5,000 and may lead to deregistration of the International Company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Return for Licensed Multi-Family Office Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Law Reform Commission / Financial Intelligence Unit (as filing agent for AML/CFT supervision)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 120 days after the end of the financial year (financial year ending 31 December unless otherwise elected)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act; persistent non-compliance may result in suspension or revocation of the financial services licence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the International Companies Act 1987, an exempt International Company is not required to file audited accounts. However, the special licence for Multi-Family Office discretionary portfolio advisory imposes a mandatory independent audit requirement irrespective of turnover or balance sheet size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the Samoa Institute of Accountants for licensed financial services activities; exempt non-licensed International Companies may use any reasonable accounting framework for internal purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must file a signed written confirmation with the Central Beneficial Ownership Register within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation. The confirmation must list all beneficial owners as of the anniversary date and flag any share transfers or changes that occurred during the previous 12 months. Share transfer updates must be reported separately to the Register within 14 days of each transfer.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for resident domestic companies; 0% effective rate for an International Company (IC) under section 200 of the International Companies Act 1987.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoa corporate income tax, dividend withholding tax, and stamp duty; no capital gains tax is imposed in Samoa. The multi-family office entity may rely on this exemption provided it confines its business to international activity, holds the required SIFA licence, and satisfies the Economic Substance Regulations (ESR).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-AR (International Company Annual Return) plus SIFA ESR-1 (Economic Substance Return); lodged electronically through the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) client portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: IC-AR: on the anniversary of incorporation, together with the annual licence fee. ESR-1: no later than 6 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., a 31 December year-end due by 30 June).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC number, registered name, financial year-end, registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Samoan registered agent as the contact; non-resident directors and shareholders are identified by name and address only, with no Samoan tax number required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify the activity under the ESR relevant-activity list (fund management, headquarters, financing/leasing, IP, distribution, banking, insurance).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'Fund Management' where the MFO exercises discretionary portfolio management; select 'Headquarters' if the entity acts as a regional coordination hub; dual selection is permissible in the SIFA portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Evidence of direction and management in Samoa, physical premises, number of employees, and annual operating expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the name of the Samoan resident director(s) present at board meetings, the lease of office space in Apia, employment contracts, and payroll records. Foreign remote staff do not satisfy the test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from the relevant activity in Samoa during the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare management fees, advisory fees, and custodian commissions even though the IC is tax-exempt; the income amount is reported to SIFA for ESR purposes, not to the Ministry of Revenue for income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sign-off by a director or authorised officer confirming accuracy of the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director must sign the declaration electronically; false declarations attract criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IC-AR: penalty of WST 500 plus 100% surcharge on the annual licence fee; risk of administrative strike-off and dissolution after 3 months. Late or false ESR-1: fixed penalty of WST 50,000 plus WST 1,000 per day of continuing default, and cancellation of the IC's tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Ministry of Revenue Corporate Income Tax Return (Form IRAS-100 / Income Tax Return for Companies), filed on paper or via the Ministry of Revenue electronic filing arrangement. Not applicable to a licensed International Company, which is outside the income tax net under ICA s.200.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the year of income (e.g., a 31 December year-end return is due 31 March); the Commissioner may grant an extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa TIN of the company; an IC does not hold a TIN unless it accidentally derives Samoa-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the MFO derives only international income, leave all IRAS boxes blank and file no return; attach a reliance letter citing ICA s.200. If any forbidden domestic-source income is derived, a TIN must be obtained within 7 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide income for a resident company; Samoa-source income for a non-resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an IC, enter zero and reference the statutory exemption; for a non-resident holding an underlying asset, only dividends, interest, and royalties sourced from Samoa fall within Box 2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year losses against current-year assessable income, capped at the statutory 5-year window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An IC cannot use this Box because it has no assessable income; do not file carryforward schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 27% corporate rate on taxable income, less credits; final balance payable on assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter nil; any payment obligation is extinguished by the exemption. A non-resident shareholder receiving a distribution pays no Samoa dividend WHT because the IC is not an income-tax-paying entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of WST 200 plus WST 50 per month or part of a month of non-filing; understatement penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall; evasive filing is a criminal offence carrying a fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 1974 for dividends paid by a resident company; reduced to 0% where the payor is an International Company because ICA s.200 exempts IC distributions from all withholding obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's double-taxation agreement network is minimal (principally the DTA with New Zealand). To claim treaty relief, a resident beneficial owner must deliver to the payer: (i) a completed Samoa Ministry of Revenue Form IRAS-WHT declaration, (ii) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, and (iii) a beneficial ownership statement. The payer must retain the approval before remitting at the reduced rate. An IC does not need such relief because no WHT is legally imposed. A foreign parent that nonetheless wishes a Samoan tax residence document for foreign tax credit purposes must apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a TRC; because an IC is tax-exempt, the TRC will normally certify residence but not liability to Samoan tax, and treaty benefits may be unavailable for lack of 'liable to tax' exposure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident rates under the Income Tax Act 1974: interest 15%, royalties 15%; treaty-reduced rates under the limited network typically reach 10% or 15%. Interest paid by an International Company on shareholder or subordinated loans and royalties paid for IP held in the MFO structure are statutorily exempt from Samoa WHT by ICA s.200.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Samoan Local File or Master File threshold is prescribed in WST; Samoa has not enacted a dedicated transfer-pricing documentation statute. The OECD/G20 BEPS country-by-country filing threshold applies to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million (approximately WST 1.2 billion). A standalone multi-family office IC is below any actionable threshold and is not required to prepare transfer-pricing documentation; however, any related-party fee (management fee or performance fee) paid to or received from an associate must satisfy the arm's length principle under the general anti-avoidance provisions of the Income Tax Act 1974 if challenged.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020 apply to every IC, including a multi-family office. Discretionary portfolio advisory for multiple private families falls within the 'fund management' relevant activity (and possibly 'headquarters' if the IC coordinates the family group). The IC must be directed and managed in Samoa, maintain adequate physical presence (premises, employees, and expenditure), file the annual ESR-1, and retain a substance file. Failure to satisfy the test negates the regulatory benefit of the exemption and triggers the penalties described above. A pure tax-exempt shell without substance will be treated as a red flag by SIFA, the FATF/EU listings process, and foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Concealment of Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoan IC as a nominee shell to conceal the identity of a Chinese or other foreign principal family; falsely declaring nil activity on the ESR; omitting discretionary advisory income; or structuring the MFO to enable the principal to evade home-jurisdiction wealth or income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act 1974: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalty assessments; SIFA will strike the IC off the register and cancel the ICA s.200 exemption; the file may be referred to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (SFIU) for anti-money-laundering action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors and the registered agent jointly and severally liable for the unpaid foreign or Samoan tax and penalties; the Ministry of Revenue may issue travel bans preventing directors from leaving Samoa; directors may be disqualified and, upon conviction, imprisoned. Professional nominee directors face licence revocation by SIFA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the multi-family office with zero employees, no Samoa premises, no board meetings in Samoa, and no core income-generating expenditure; using only a mail-forwarding address; repeated default of ESR-1 filings; presenting the IC to counter-parties as a substantive asset-holding vehicle when it is not.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalty of WST 50,000, daily continuing penalty of WST 1,000, mandatory striking-off and dissolution by the Registrar of International Companies; re-registration barred for 5 years; referral to the EU/OECD harmful-tax-practices process increases the jurisdiction's risk rating.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false economic substance declarations are personally liable for the WST 50,000 penalty and restitution; the court may impose director disqualification and a travel prohibition; in flagrant cases, directors face fraud charges carrying imprisonment of up to 7 years under Samoa's Crimes Act 2013.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing discretionary portfolio management, custody wires, SWIFT interbank payments, or account administration for multiple private client families without the required SIFA special financial services licence; processing client wires without KYC/CDD; handling proceeds of tax evasion or foreign corruption; failing to appoint a Samoan AML compliance officer and reporting suspicious transactions to the SFIU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2007 (as amended): fines up to WST 1,000,000 for a body corporate; freezing and confiscation of assets; revocation of the international company's licence and a mandatory cease-and-desist order; the entity is listed on the public sanctions register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are criminally liable for money laundering (imprisonment up to 14 years) and for operating an unlicensed financial business (imprisonment up to 5 years); personal civil liability for client losses and restitution; travel bans and asset freezing orders may be imposed pending prosecution; the SFIU may also refer directors to foreign authorities for coordinated action.
